newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 9.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 9.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Lumber sales were sluggish as traders spent Monday and Tuesday plugging back into the market after the long holiday weekend in the United States, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. Southern Pine was an exception, as buyers stepped in to replenish inventories, the lumber reporting agency said.

Many items in other species were easily bought on counters, as buyers felt no urgency to take more than immediate needs. In structural panels, plywood producers dropped sheathing prices to jump-start sales. An uptick in sales led to small OSB gains.
Most Western S-P-F prices were vulnerable to small counters but producers were unwilling or didn't need to seek business aggressively. They reported steady but unspectacular sales.
Western Std&Btr 2x4 sold as low as $355. Most producers hung with quotes in the $360-365 range. Short order files forced a few stud mills to open to counters, Random Lengths said.
Eastern S-P-F made a comeback after last week's slowness.

Eastern prices were unchanged. With mill vacations approaching the peak, many buyers saw the futility of bargain hunting or attempting counters. Secondaries took most of the retail fill-ins, particularly those wanting quick shipment.

Southern Pine traders got right back to business after the long weekend. Prices rose, with some mills pricing aggressively. Producers booked into the week of July 21 on popular items, but some 2x12 was still available for realtively quick shipment.
Inland sales were measured as producers waited for customers to arrive for a gathering in Coeur d'Alene. Std&Btr 2x4 was especially soft in both Hem-Fir and Fir-Larch.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir prices held or edged down in thin trading. The post-holiday rally some producers had anticipated failed to materialize, and some accepted small counters. Prompt-shipping, highly specified loads moved best. Hem-fir studs were flat, while Fir lost $2.

Southern Pine plywood markets took a firmer tone as buyers came back from the long weekend with needs to fill. One westside major sold heavy volumes and extended its order file into the week of July 28. It took lower prices to start the momentum, but prices firmed close to last week's levels, the agency said.

Western plywood sheathing prices were soft but buyers cleaned up prompt wood at some mills and pushed shipping times into the week of July 14. Mills took a firmer stance as they rebuilt order files. Downward pressure was greatest on 1/2-inch 4- and 5-ply, but these items were the focus of buying. The 23/32-inch underlayment traded in the $530-535 range.

OSB sales picked up in a few areas, prompting a number of mills to raise quotes. North Central producers had the most success, while mills in other regions often had to trade off the higher asking levels to maintain volumes. One large mill in western Canada announced an 11-day maintenance shutdown.
